headline: Medium risk: ComfyUI can feed generated files into pdf.js, creating a plausible prompt/data cascade, but direct injection and compliance harms are limited by offline/local surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can emit workflows/files and pdf.js reads PDF files, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry malicious instructions into a downstream parser. However, neither profile shows a shared channel by default, and both are local/offline-oriented, so the pathway is unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF the operator copies ComfyUI-generated content into a PDF that pdf.js then opens
IF a shared filesystem or manual copy-paste bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge for untrusted content
Open only trusted PDFs in pdf.js
Review generated files before handing them to pdf.js

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, models, and workflows, while pdf.js touches PDF documents. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, OAuth principal, or network exfiltration path, so leakage is limited to an unusual local file-sharing setup.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory containing sensitive PDFs or model assets
IF the operator exports ComfyUI outputs into files that pdf.js later opens
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Store sensitive PDFs outside any shared workspace
Avoid placing model checkpoints and documents in the same folder
Delete temporary exports after review

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, and pdf.js only exposes PDF-file handling with browser-based tests. There is no overlapping write authority or shared mutable resource in the profiles, so a capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF either profile is changed to grant both agents write access to the same directory
IF an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state or locking-free git access
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI read-only with respect to shared assets
Do not grant pdf.js filesystem write access
Avoid shared git worktrees
Add orchestration locks if write access is later introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can produce workflows and generated assets that pdf.js may consume as documents, so A's output can become B's input. Because pdf.js is a document processor and no verification step is shown, a mistaken or malicious upstream artifact could cascade into incorrect downstream rendering or decisions.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are treated as authoritative documents by pdf.js
IF pdf.js is used downstream without a human verification step
mitigations: Insert a manual review step between agents
Require file-type validation before pdf.js opens outputs
Use a quarantine folder for new ComfyUI artifacts
Reject any non-PDF artifact before downstream processing

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles do not indicate PHI, EU PII, residency constraints, or retention-policy mismatches. ComfyUI is offline-capable and pdf.js has no network egress, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced from the pair alone.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into either agent
IF an external policy requires residency or retention controls not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention and deletion rules before use
Run a quick data-classification check on inputs
Use separate storage for regulated documents
